transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thanks for seeing me. I’m here because lately, well, I’ll get off a long shift at the shop and just end up eating way more than I ever planned to. Like, I'll put away a full fast-food meal on the way home, and then I'll just keep going with snacks, and basically whatever else is in the fridge. 

It's all in one sitting, just eating until it's gone. It's been bothering me a lot, so I figured I should probably talk to somebody about it.

After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to compensate or make up for what you've eaten — like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or restricting food afterwards?

Yeah, I do. Sometimes after I eat way too much like that, I... well, I'll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Or I'll take some laxatives. I just get really scared of what all that food is going to do to me, so I feel like I have to get it out of my system.
How often would you say these episodes happen — where you eat a lot and then make yourself throw up or use laxatives? Are we talking about a few times a week, or how frequently?

Well, it's pretty much every week. Most weeks I have at least one night where I just eat way too much and then try to undo it, you know? Like making myself throw up, or taking those laxatives. Sometimes I'll just skip meals the next day or push myself really hard at the gym instead. And, uh, it's been happening like this for several months now.

latest_inference.note: Patient describes recurrent binge eating episodes followed by compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative use, fasting, excessive exercise) occurring at least weekly for several months. This is consistent with Bulimia Nervosa (F50.81). F50.82 (Binge Eating Disorder) is ruled out because the patient engages in regular compensatory/purging behaviors, which is the defining feature of Bulimia Nervosa rather than BED.
